title: How to get A*A*A*
caption: A*A*A* isn't magic, it's method. 5 research-backed habits, no 5am cold showers required. Save this for revision season 📌

slides.headline: How to get {A*A*A*}
slides.sub: Only 9.6% of A-level grades were an A* in 2026. Here's what the research says works.

slides.headline: Stop rereading. {Start testing.}
slides.body: Practice testing is one of only two techniques rated “high utility” in a review of 10 study methods.

slides.headline: Space it {out}
slides.body: Revisit each topic over weeks, not one cram. Spaced practice was the other “high utility” technique.

slides.headline: Past papers, {exam conditions}
slides.body: Timed. Closed book. Phone in another room. Then mark it strictly against the mark scheme.

slides.headline: Steal the examiner's {words}
slides.body: For every lost mark, copy the exact mark-scheme phrase that would have scored it. That's your revision list.

slides.headline: {Mix} your topics
slides.body: Shuffle question types instead of 20 of the same. In maths studies, mixed practice beat blocked practice on later tests.

slides.headline: Answer. Tap {Mark}. Get feedback.
slides.body: Real past-paper questions, marked instantly. Your first marked answer unlocks a predicted grade.

sources.title: GCE A level results summer 2026 – press notice
sources.claim: 9.6% of A level results were awarded A* in 2026 (9.4% in 2025). UK-wide, provisional.

sources.title: Improving Students' Learning With Effective Learning Techniques (Psychological Science in the Public Interest 14(1), 4–58) – press summary
sources.claim: Of 10 techniques reviewed, practice testing and distributed practice received the highest (high) utility rating; rereading, highlighting and summarisation were rated low utility.

sources.title: Spacing effects in learning: a temporal ridgeline of optimal retention
sources.claim: With 1,350+ participants, the gap between study sessions affected retention; the optimal gap grew with how long you need to remember (about 20–40% of a 1-week delay, 5–10% of a 1-year delay).

sources.publisher: Instructional Science (summary by M. S. Glessmer)
sources.title: The shuffling of mathematics practice problems boosts learning (Instructional Science 35, 481–498) – summary
sources.claim: Blocked practice scored higher during practice, but on a later test covering all topics, students who mixed problems clearly outperformed those who blocked.

sources.title: The Effect of Interleaving Practice
sources.claim: Interleaved (mixed) practice improved later test performance compared with blocked practice.
